subject: Mathematics
title: Sets: Chapter Introduction
summary: A set is a well-defined collection: anyone can decide whether a thing belongs to it or not. The chapter builds the language of sets that the rest of mathematics uses.
keyPoints: A **set** is a **well-defined** collection of objects.
"Best cricketers" is not a set; "months starting with J" = {January, June, July} is.
Notation: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}; **4 ∈ A** (4 belongs to A).
Sets can be **empty**, **finite** or **infinite**; **union** and **intersection** are shown on **Venn diagrams**.

sections.h: What makes a collection a set

blocks.p: A collection is **well-defined** when, for any object, we can say for certain whether it belongs to the collection or not.

list: Sets are named with capital letters, elements are written inside curly brackets { }.
**Set-builder form:** A = {x : x is an even natural number, x ≤ 10}.
**4 ∈ A** means 4 belongs to A; **5 ∉ A** means 5 does not.
